candidate.codeAnchorPolicy: codeCommit is the authoritative candidate demo source identity for fresh V00-V05. Following handoff/source-target/source-pin and Docs/AssemblyShadow review commits are metadata-only under the committed source verifier.

reproduction.preservationPolicy: Do not move this branch for the managed-cache Primary correction. Preserve the unfixed count behavior and existing validation handoff.

performanceReference.policy: Preserve its own committed old-profile pins. Do not install the candidate runtime into this reference.

primaryValidation.scope: Authenticated Apple Bee graph planning, reversible declared-input retention, fail-closed retention controls, managed changed-action/cache-hit provenance regressions, and portable/host-Clang tool regressions. Not Unity, Apple Player, current-build managed cache acceptance, runtime, or M08 acceptance.

retentionRepair.policy: Retain every declared native source by raw SHA-256 and raw length while separating content identity from reversible storage representation. Generated C/C++/ObjC sources use content-addressed zlib-v1 only when smaller; semantic request/DAG/PCH/header/response/plist evidence stays raw by default. Successful attempts independently authenticate the retained store before finalization.

managedCacheRepair.failure: Fresh native provenance and retention passed, but the managed verifier required a changed Bee graph even when the exact required Player Csc/ILPP chain and DLL outputs were legitimately reused from an unchanged Bee cache.
managedCacheRepair.policy: At begin, retain bounded exact reusable Player Csc chains from pre-existing Bee DAGs, including graph/action, response closure, compiler dependencies/tools, Csc output, and reachable downstream DLL bytes. At end, require all retained cache evidence to remain byte-identical and require exactly one chain to reach the exact path/hash/size of the DLL captured as an input to the fresh Player. Prefer a unique changed-graph proof when present. Cache proof never claims fresh Csc execution and is not the legacy prior-proof reuse route.
